section_summary: This section brings together U.S. diplomatic and intelligence reporting on Japanese organizations, news correspondents, espionage allegations, and relief work in Argentina. It includes correspondence about a Japanese cinema owner's letter, allegations against Noboru Hara, interrogations of former ambassador Shu Tomii and correspondent Masao Tuda, and later reports on travel, relief shipments, and the reorganization of the Japanese Association of Argentina. Pages 234–247 and 248–261 contain two copies of the same Tokyo despatch and its three enclosures.

subfiles.title: Request for information on German and Japanese organizations in Argentina
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: The embassy requests information on organizations' subversive activities, official connections, and subsidies.
subfiles.summary: Lists organizations and asks for prompt, separate reports on evidence about each.

subfiles.title: Handwritten note on releasing information
subfiles.about: An unidentified writer asks whether information can be furnished.
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten query about providing information; much of the text is illegible.

subfiles.title: Review of documents for possible transfer to Argentina
subfiles.from: FC, Mr. Bradford
subfiles.about: Bradford requests careful review before documents are given to the Perón government.
subfiles.summary: Asks Hoyt to decide whether attached material concerning Unión Germánica en la Argentina should be released.

subfiles.title: Letter from São Paulo to Japanese agent in Buenos Aires
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: The embassy reports a Japanese letter addressed to Ryohei Gashu and forwards photostats.
subfiles.summary: A cursory examination found questions about Japanese films and newspapers. The embassy notes Gashu's alleged espionage role and seeks further assessment of the letter.

subfiles.title: Japanese letter from Nippaku Cinema
subfiles.from: Masaichi Saito, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The cinema owner writes to Gashu about Japanese films and conditions among Japanese residents in São Paulo.
subfiles.summary: Two pages of the Japanese-language letter forwarded with the Buenos Aires embassy despatch.

subfiles.title: Identification and account of the Nippaku Cinema letter
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consul General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: The consul identifies the writer and recounts the letter's references to films and Japanese terrorist societies.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Masaichi Saito as writer and summarizes his proposed film exchange and comments on threats in São Paulo.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Tokyo information on Japanese subversive activities
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Tokyo despatch 797 and permits discretionary sharing with Argentine authorities.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Tokyo's findings and says further requested information will follow.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal notice for restricted item
subfiles.from: National Archives
subfiles.about: The form records withdrawal of a restricted Tokyo item from the file.
subfiles.summary: Identifies despatch 797 as withdrawn for restricted information.

subfiles.title: Noboru Hara and Nippon Gawa
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: The embassy transmits its note to Argentina concerning Noboru Hara.
subfiles.summary: Covers a note verbale answering Argentina's inquiry into Hara's alleged connection with Nippon Gawa.

subfiles.title: Note verbale on Noboru Hara
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.to: Argentine Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Worship
subfiles.about: The embassy details allegations linking Hara to maritime espionage and Japanese propaganda.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Hara allegedly directed port intelligence agents, used news agencies in Madrid to forward information, and was proposed for repatriation.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form
subfiles.from: Department of State Central Records
subfiles.about: The form designates an attached copy to replace a missing original action copy.
subfiles.summary: Marks the attached despatch copy as the file's record copy.

subfiles.title: Request for information regarding Japanese subversive activities in Argentina, first copy
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Tokyo forwards an interrogation, a biography, and a report concerning Japanese activities in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Introduces three enclosures about former ambassador Tomii and Domei correspondent Tuda.

subfiles.title: Interrogation of Baron Shu Tomii, first copy
subfiles.from: U.S. Army Forces, Pacific, Compilation Branch
subfiles.about: Tomii answers questions about Japanese associations, embassy finances, attachés, and alleged intelligence contacts.
subfiles.summary: Tomii denies formal embassy control of several associations and knowledge of a Black Dragon branch. He discusses bank and legation handling of embassy funds, attachés, and a paid inquiry into the treatment of Japanese residents in Brazil.

subfiles.title: Biographical sketch of Baron Shu Tomii, first copy
subfiles.from: U.S. Army Forces, Pacific, Compilation Branch
subfiles.about: The sketch lists Tomii's education, diplomatic appointments, and decorations.
subfiles.summary: Traces Tomii's career through postings in China, the United States, Britain, Canada, Germany, and Argentina.

subfiles.title: Report on Masao Tuda, first copy
subfiles.from: F. G. Tillman, FBI liaison officer
subfiles.to: Colonel W. S. Wood, Civil Intelligence Section
subfiles.about: The report describes Tuda's Domei work and alleged intelligence connections in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Based largely on Tuda's interview, it describes news agency cables carrying military and political information, embassy and attaché contacts, bank financing, and Argentine police inquiries. It also identifies people linked to particular information gathering assignments and records Tuda's denials or qualifications.

subfiles.title: Request for information regarding Japanese subversive activities in Argentina, record copy
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: A clearer copy of despatch 797 forwards three enclosures on Tomii and Tuda.
subfiles.summary: Reports that more information is being obtained and will be transmitted.

subfiles.title: Interrogation of Baron Shu Tomii, record copy
subfiles.from: U.S. Army Forces, Pacific, Compilation Branch
subfiles.about: Tomii discusses Japanese community organizations, embassy funds, attachés, and named contacts.
subfiles.summary: Tomii denies knowledge of a Black Dragon organization in Argentina and rejects claims of formal links between the embassy and several local associations. He explains embassy finances and comments on allegations involving Tuda, Fernandez, Kobayashi, Perrone, and Murai. Investigators recommend further interviews.

subfiles.title: Biographical sketch of Baron Shu Tomii, record copy
subfiles.from: U.S. Army Forces, Pacific, Compilation Branch
subfiles.about: The sketch records Tomii's diplomatic career and decorations.
subfiles.summary: Lists education, successive foreign and ministry appointments, ambassadorial service in Argentina, and Japanese decorations.

subfiles.title: Report on Masao Tuda, record copy
subfiles.from: F. G. Tillman, FBI liaison officer
subfiles.to: Colonel W. S. Wood, Civil Intelligence Section
subfiles.about: The report examines Tuda's intelligence activities, financing, contacts, and interview statements.
subfiles.summary: It says Japanese news correspondents in Buenos Aires sent information on U.S. military and economic matters and describes Tuda's use of Domei cable facilities for attachés' messages. Tuda explains his arrests, working methods, financing through the Yokohama Specie Bank, and contacts with embassy officials and intermediaries. The report records both allegations and Tuda's denials about paid informants and particular assignments.

subfiles.title: Forwarding intelligence material to the Department of State
subfiles.from: Chief, Source Control Branch, Central Intelligence Group
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Department of State
subfiles.about: The branch forwards material obtained from sources it considers reliable.
subfiles.summary: Cover memorandum transmitting an attached intelligence report.

subfiles.title: Report on Antonio José de Silva (Souza)
subfiles.from: Central Intelligence Group
subfiles.about: The report alleges a traveler's past work for a Japanese shipping line and gives his planned U.S. itinerary.
subfiles.summary: Identifies his Argentine passport and visa, alleges he arranged Japanese agents' entry into Argentina, and notes planned stops before sailing from San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Forwarding report on Antonio José de Silva
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Nanking
subfiles.about: The Department sends the intelligence report to Nanking and comments on its surveillance suggestion.
subfiles.summary: States that no U.S. surveillance occurred because no direct request for action was made.

subfiles.title: Japanese relief organizations as possible vehicles for imperialism
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Tokyo reports approved channels for relief shipments from Argentine organizations to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Public Health and Welfare Section explains that LARA receives and distributes approved relief supplies under review. It describes how Argentine welfare groups could send funds or goods through LARA and mentions a representative's planned visit to Brazil and possibly Argentina.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form for Tokyo despatch 1047
subfiles.from: Department of State Central Records
subfiles.about: The form designates a copy of Tokyo despatch 1047 as the record copy.
subfiles.summary: Replaces an original action copy that was not returned for filing.

subfiles.title: Further report on Japanese subversive activities in Argentina
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Tokyo transmits a report compiled from interrogations of Japanese returnees from Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch for a report titled “Japanese Subversive Activities in Argentina.”

subfiles.title: Forwarding Tokyo despatch 1047 to Buenos Aires
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Tokyo's interrogation report for the embassy's information.
subfiles.summary: Sends a copy of despatch 1047 and its report on former Japanese diplomatic staff.

subfiles.title: Reorganization of the Japanese Association of Argentina
subfiles.from: R. Kenneth Oakley, U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: The embassy reports the association's renewed activities, required safeguards, and leadership change.
subfiles.summary: An Argentine decree permits the association to resume charitable work, including support for its tuberculosis sanatorium, subject to revised statutes. After embassy concern about elected president Kichihei Hoshi, Argentine officials informally sought his resignation; vice president Kosei Shimizukawa assumed the presidency.
